tool_input.description: Show uncommitted changes and new files

result:
I found one new spot that matches the flagged rule, but I didn't change it because I don't think it's an access check.

The only new `.role` comparison in the uncommitted change is in `apps/react-vite/src/features/users/utils/filter-users.ts:24`:

```ts
if (role !== 'ALL' && user.role !== role) return false;
```

It filters the list of users by the role selected in the dropdown. It doesn't check what the signed-in user may do. Routing it through `<Authorization>` or `checkAccess` would check the current user's roles, which is the wrong question here, so I left the code as it is.

I also checked the other changed files. `users-list.tsx`, `delete-user.tsx` and `users-csv.ts` don't compare any role, and the only current-user check (`user.data?.id === id` in `delete-user.tsx`) is an ownership check that already lives in the component.

If the reviewer meant this filter, I can change it, but the only option I see is a different spelling of the same comparison. Tell me if you want that, or whether the reviewer had a different line in mind.

I didn't run tests, lint or the app, and I made no commits.
